Z_{t}^{u}=0,\quad\sigma_{t}^{u}\widetilde{\pi}_{t}^{u}=\eta^{u}\theta_{t}^{u}\end{cases} $$

is a solution to the BSDE (4.3). The convergence results (2.7) thus follows from the boundedness of $\eta$ and $\theta_{t}$ .

### 4.2 Proofs for Section 3.1

We now present the proof of the characterization result for the $n$ -player game. This section consists of the proof for Theorem 3.1 and two auxiliary lemmas: Lemma 4.1 and Lemma 4.2.

#### Proof of Theorem 3.1.

Assume that $(\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n})_{i\in\{1,\dots,n\}}$ is a Nash equilibrium of the problem (2.2). First note that our assumptions on $\sigma_{t}^{i}$ , $\sigma_{t}^{*i}$ , and $\mu^{i}_{t}$ imply that $\overline{X}_{t}^{i}\in\mathbb{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R},\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n})$ . Let $\mathcal{T}$ be the set of all $\mathbb{F}^{n}$ –stopping times in $[0,T]$ . Define the following family of random variables:

$$ \mathcal{J}^{i,\pi}(\tau):=\mathbb{E}\Big[-\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}\left(\int_{\tau}^{T}\pi_{s}\cdot(\Sigma_{s}^{i}\theta_{s}^{i}\mathrm{d}s+\sigma_{s}^{i}\mathrm{d}W_{s}^{i}+\sigma_{s}^{*i}\mathrm{d}W_{s}^{*})-\rho(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})\right)}\big|\mathcal{F}_{\tau}^{n}\Big], $$

and let

$$ \mathcal{V}^{i}(\tau):=\esssup_{\pi\in\mathcal{A}^{i}}\mathcal{J}^{i,\pi}(\tau)\text{ for all }\tau\in\mathcal{T},\text{ so that }\mathcal{V}^{i}(0)=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}(\xi^{i}-\rho\overline{\xi}^{i})}V_{0}^{i,n}((\widetilde{\pi}^{j})_{j\neq i}). $$

Now let

$$ \upbeta_{\tau}^{i,\pi}:=\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}\int_{0}^{\tau}\pi_{u}\cdot(\Sigma_{u}^{i}\theta_{u}^{i}\mathrm{d}u+\sigma_{u}^{i}\mathrm{d}W_{u}^{i}+\sigma_{u}^{*i}\mathrm{d}W_{u}^{*})}. $$

Then it can be checked as in the proof of [17, Lemma 4.13] that for all $\pi\in\mathcal{A}_{i}$ ,

$$ \upbeta_{\tau_{1}}^{i,\pi}\mathcal{V}^{i}(\tau_{1})\geq\mathbb{E}\big[\upbeta_{\tau_{2}}^{i,\pi}\mathcal{V}^{i}(\tau_{2})\big|\mathcal{F}_{\tau_{2}}^{n}\big]\text{ for all stopping times }\tau_{1}\leq\tau_{2}, $$

and by [27, Proposition I.3.14], the process $\mathcal{V}^{i}$ has a càdlàg modification again denoted $(\mathcal{V}^{i}_{t})_{t\in[0,T]}$ . Moreover, this process also satisfies (4.4), so that for any $\pi\in\mathcal{A}_{i}$ , the process $\beta^{i,\pi}\mathcal{V}^{i}$ is a $\mathbb{P}$ -supermartingale. Now the definition of Nash equilibrium implies that $\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n}$ is optimal for agent $i$ . In other words,

$$ \mathcal{V}_{0}^{i}=\sup_{\pi\in\mathcal{A}_{i}}\mathbb{E}\big[-\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}(X_{T}^{i,\pi}-\xi^{i}-\rho(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i}))}\big]=\mathbb{E}\big[-\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}(X_{T}^{i,\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n}}-\xi^{i}-\rho(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i}))}\big]. $$

The above implies that $\upbeta^{i,\widetilde{\pi}}\mathcal{V}^{i}$ is a $\mathbb{P}$ -martingale, where we write $\upbeta^{i,\widetilde{\pi}}$ as a shorthand notation for $\upbeta^{i,\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n}}$ . Denote $\tilde{M}^{i}:=\upbeta^{i,\tilde{\pi}}\mathcal{V}^{i}$ . We now proceed to show that the adapted and continuous process

$$ \gamma_{t}^{i}=X_{t}^{\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n}}-\xi^{i}+\eta^{i}\ln(-\tilde{M}_{t}^{i}),\quad t\in[0,T] $$

solves a BSDE. Note already that by definition of $\mathcal{V}^{i}_{t}$ and $\tilde{M}^{i}_{t}$ , we have

$$ V_{0}^{i,n}((\widetilde{\pi}^{j,n})_{j\neq i})=-\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}(\xi^{i}-\rho\overline{\xi}^{i}-\gamma_{0}^{i})}. $$

This proves the representation of $V^{i,n}_{0}((\widetilde{\pi}^{j,n})_{j\neq i})$ .

We first need to check that $\gamma^{i}$ is indeed in $\mathbb{S}^{1}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{n})$ . On the one hand, using Jensen’s inequality, we have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}\mathbb{E}\big[X_{T}^{i,\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n}}-\xi^{i}-\rho(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\big]\leq\ln(-\tilde{M}_{t}^{i}). $$

On the other hand, by definition of $\mathcal{V}^{i}$ , we have $-\tilde{M}_{t}^{i}=-\upbeta^{i,\widetilde{\pi}}_{t}\mathcal{V}^{i}_{t}\leq\upbeta^{i,\widetilde{\pi}}_{t}\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\rho}{\eta^{i}}(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}]$ . Thus, using the inequality $\ln(x)\leq x$ we have

$$ \displaystyle\ln(-\tilde{M}^{i}_{t}) \displaystyle\leq\ln(\upbeta^{i,\widetilde{\pi}}_{t})+\ln\Big(\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\rho}{\eta^{i}}(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}]\Big) \displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}\int_{0}^{t}\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n}_{u}\cdot(\Sigma_{u}^{i}\theta_{u}^{i}\mathrm{d}u+\sigma_{u}^{i}\mathrm{d}W_{u}^{i}+\sigma_{u}^{*i}\mathrm{d}W_{u}^{*})+\mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\rho}{\eta^{i}}(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\big]. $$

Now, combining this with Equation 4.6 and the definition of $\upbeta_{t}^{i,\tilde{\pi}}$ , we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}|\ln(-\tilde{M}^{i}_{t})|\Big] \displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\frac{1}{\eta_{i}}\mathbb{E}\big[|X_{t}^{\tilde{\pi}^{i,n}}-\xi^{i}-\rho(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})|\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\big]\Big] \displaystyle\quad+\mathbb{E}\big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\frac{1}{\eta_{i}}|X_{t}^{\tilde{\pi}^{i,n}}-\xi^{i}|\big]+\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\rho}{\eta^{i}}(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\big]\Big] \displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{\eta_{i}}\mathbb{E}\big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbb{E}[|X_{T}^{\tilde{\pi}^{i,n}}|\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}]\big]+\mathbb{E}\big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}|X_{t}^{\tilde{\pi}^{i,n}}|\big]+2\mathbb{E}[\xi^{i}] \displaystyle\quad+\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\frac{1}{\eta_{i}}\mathbb{E}\big[|\rho(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})|\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\big]\Big]+\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\rho}{\eta^{i}}(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\big]\Big]. $$

It is then sufficient to bound the last term. By Jensen’s and Hölder’s inequalities we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\rho}{\eta^{i}}(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\big]\Big]\leq\frac{1}{n-1}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\rho}{\eta_{i}}\frac{\lambda_{ij}}{\beta_{n}}\xi^{j}}\big]^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\rho}{\eta_{i}}\frac{\lambda_{ij}}{\beta_{n}}X_{T}^{\widetilde{\pi}^{j}}}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\big]^{\frac{1}{2}}\Big]. $$

By the admissibility condition on $\pi$ , it follows that $\ln(-\tilde{M}^{i})\in\mathbb{S}^{1}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{n})$ . It thus follows that $\gamma^{i}\in\mathbb{S}^{1}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{n})$ for every $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ . For an arbitrary $\pi\in\mathcal{A}_{i}$ , define

$$ M_{t}^{i,\pi}:=\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}(X_{t}^{\pi}-\xi^{i}-\gamma_{t}^{i})}=\tilde{M}_{t}^{i}\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}(X_{t}^{\pi}-X_{t}^{\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n}})}. $$

It follows from the same argument as in [17, Theorem 4.7 2(b)] that $M^{i,\pi}$ is a supermartingale. Now by Equation 4.5, Doob–Meyer decomposition and Itô’s formula, there is $(\zeta^{i},\zeta^{*i})\in\mathbb{H}^{2}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^{nd},\mathbb{F})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F})$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{d}\gamma_{t}^{i}=-b_{t}^{i}\mathrm{d}t+\sum\limits_{j=1}^{n}\zeta_{t}^{ij}\cdot\mathrm{d}W_{t}^{j}+\zeta^{*i}_{t}\mathrm{d}W_{t}^{*}. $$

We will proceed by first computing $b^{i}$ , $\gamma^{i}$ and $\widetilde{\pi}^{i}$ , and next deriving the BSDEs satisfied by $(\gamma^{i},\zeta^{i},\zeta^{*i})$ .

By Itô’s formula, we have

$$ \displaystyle-\mathrm{d}\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}(X_{t}^{\pi}-\xi^{i}-\gamma_{t}^{i})} \displaystyle=\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}(X_{t}^{\pi}-\xi^{i}-\gamma_{t}^{i})}\cdot\Bigg\{\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}\bigg(\left(\sigma_{t}^{i}\pi_{t}^{i}\right)\cdot\mathrm{d}W_{t}^{i}+\sum\limits_{j=1}^{n}\zeta_{t}^{ij}\cdot\mathrm{d}W_{t}^{j}+\left(\sigma_{t}^{*i}\cdot\pi_{t}^{i}+\zeta_{t}^{*i}\right)\mathrm{d}W_{t}^{*}\bigg) \displaystyle\qquad+\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}\left(b_{t}^{i}+\pi_{t}^{i}\cdot\Sigma_{t}^{i}\theta_{t}^{i}\right)\mathrm{d}t+\frac{1}{(\eta^{i})^{2}}\bigg(\sigma_{t}^{i}\pi_{t}^{i}\cdot\zeta_{t}^{ii}+\sigma_{t}^{*i}\pi_{t}^{i}\zeta^{*i}_{t}\bigg)\mathrm{d}t \displaystyle\qquad-\frac{1}{2(\eta^{i})^{2}}\bigg(|\sigma_{t}^{i}\pi_{t}|^{2}+|\sigma_{t}^{*i}\pi_{t}|^{2}+\sum\limits_{j=1}^{n}|\zeta_{t}^{ij}|^{2}+|\zeta_{t}^{*i}|^{2}\bigg)\mathrm{d}t\Bigg\}. $$

Using the supermartingale property of $M^{i,\pi}$ , the martingale property of $\tilde{M}^{i}$ , together with (4.8), keeping in mind that $\Sigma_{t}^{i}:=(\sigma_{t}^{i},\sigma_{t}^{*i})$ , and writing $\zeta^{i}_{t}:=(\zeta^{ii}_{t},\zeta^{*i}_{t})$ , we get

$$ \displaystyle b_{t}^{i}\leq\frac{1}{2\eta_{i}}\lvert{\Sigma_{t}^{i}}^{\top}\pi_{t}^{i}-(\zeta_{t}^{i}+\eta^{i}\theta_{t}^{i})\rvert^{2}+\frac{1}{2\eta^{i}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}|\zeta_{t}^{ij}|^{2}-\frac{\eta_{i}}{2}|\theta_{t}^{i}|^{2}-\zeta_{t}^{i}\cdot\theta_{t}^{i}, $$

and

$$ \displaystyle b_{t}^{i}=\frac{1}{2\eta^{i}}\lvert{\Sigma_{t}^{i}}^{\top}\tilde{\pi}_{t}^{i}-(\zeta_{t}^{i}+\eta^{i}\theta_{t}^{i})\rvert^{2}+\frac{1}{2\eta^{i}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}|\zeta_{t}^{ij}|^{2}-\frac{\eta^{i}}{2}|\theta_{t}^{i}|^{2}-\zeta_{t}^{i}\cdot\theta_{t}^{i}. $$

Thus, $\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n}_{t}$ minimizes the function (in $\pi^{i}$ ) on the right hand side of (4.9). Therefore, we can express $\widetilde{\pi}_{t}^{i,n}$ and $b_{t}^{i}$ as follow:

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{\pi}_{t}^{i} \displaystyle=\left({\Sigma_{t}^{i}\Sigma_{t}^{i}}^{\top}\right)^{-1}{\Sigma_{t}^{i}}P_{t}^{i}\big(\zeta_{t}^{i}+\eta^{i}\theta_{t}^{i}\big), \displaystyle b_{t}^{i} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{2\eta^{i}}\mathrm{dist}\Big(\zeta_{t}^{i}+\eta_{i}\theta_{t}^{i},\Sigma_{t}^{i}A^{i}\Big)^{2}+\frac{1}{2\eta^{i}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}|\zeta_{t}^{ij}|^{2}-\frac{\eta^{i}}{2}|\theta_{t}^{i}|^{2}-\zeta_{t}^{i}\cdot\theta_{t}^{i}. $$

Therefore, $(\gamma^{i},\zeta^{i},\zeta^{*i})\in\mathbb{S}^{1}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^{nd},\mathbb{F})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F})$ solves the BSDE

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}\mathrm{d}\gamma_{t}^{i}&=\bigg(\zeta_{t}^{i}\cdot\theta_{t}^{i}+\frac{\eta^{i}}{2}|\theta_{t}^{i}|^{2}-\frac{1}{2\eta^{i}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}|\zeta_{t}^{ij}|^{2}-\frac{1}{2\eta^{i}}\Big|(I-P_{t}^{i})\left(\zeta_{t}^{i}+\eta^{i}\theta_{t}^{i}\right)\Big|^{2}\bigg)\mathrm{d}t\\

\gamma_{T}^{i}&=\rho(\overline{X}_{T}^{i}-\overline{\xi}^{i})=\rho\sum_{j\neq i}{\lambda_{ij}^{n}\int_{0}^{T}\widetilde{\pi}^{j}_{s}\cdot\big\{\Sigma_{s}^{j}\theta^{j}_{s}\mathrm{d}s+\sigma_{s}^{j}\mathrm{d}W_{s}^{j}+\sigma_{s}^{j*}\mathrm{d}W_{s}^{*}\big\}}.\end{split} $$

#### Lemma 4.1.

For any $t\in[0,T]$ , fixed $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ , the map

$$ \displaystyle H_{\alpha,\beta}(x)=x+\frac{1}{n-1}{\sigma_{t}^{*i}}^{\top}\left(\Sigma_{t}^{i}{\Sigma_{t}^{i}}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\Sigma_{t}^{i}\cdot P_{t}^{i}\left(\begin{pmatrix}\alpha\\
x\end{pmatrix}+\beta\right) $$

is a bijection on $\mathbb{R}$ for every $i$ . Furthermore, its inverse is a contraction.

#### Proof.

Fix $t\in[0,T]$ and $i$ . $H_{\alpha}(\cdot)$ is a bijection if and only if the map

$$ \displaystyle M^{y}(x)=y-\frac{1}{n-1}{\sigma_{t}^{*i}}^{\top}\left(\Sigma_{t}^{i}{\Sigma_{t}^{i}}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\Sigma_{t}^{i}\cdot P_{t}^{i}\left(\begin{pmatrix}\alpha\\
x\end{pmatrix}+\beta\right) $$

has a unique fixed point. Notice that since the projection operator is $1$ –Lipschitz,

$$ \displaystyle\lvert M^{y}(x)-M^{y}(x^{\prime})\rvert\leq\frac{1}{n-1}\Big|{{\sigma_{t}^{*i}}^{\top}\left(\Sigma_{t}^{i}{\Sigma_{t}^{i}}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\Sigma_{t}^{i}}\Big|\lvert x-x^{\prime}\rvert. $$

It is thus sufficient to show that $\Big|{{\sigma_{t}^{*i}}^{\top}\left(\Sigma_{t}^{i}{\Sigma_{t}^{i}}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\Sigma_{t}^{i}}\Big|<1$ . For notational convenience, let us omit all $t$ subscripts. First notice that $\Sigma^{i}{\Sigma^{i}}^{\top}=\sigma^{i}\sigma^{i}+\sigma^{*i}{\sigma^{*i}}^{\top}$ . Using the Sherman-Morrison formula, we have that

$$ \displaystyle\left(\Sigma^{i}{\Sigma^{i}}^{\top}\right)^{-1}=\sigma^{-i}\sigma^{-i}-\frac{\sigma^{-i}\sigma^{-i}\sigma^{*i}{\sigma^{*i}}^{\top}\sigma^{-i}\sigma^{-i}}{1+{\sigma^{*i}}^{\top}\sigma^{-i}\sigma^{-i}\sigma^{*i}}, $$

and

#### Lemma 4.2.

Consider the map $\upphi_{t}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{n}$ introduced in the statement of Theorem 3.1 and defined component-wise below as

&\qquad\qquad P^{j}\left(\begin{pmatrix}Z^{jj}\\

## 5 General backward propagation of chaos theorem: proof of Theorem 2.11

In this section we present backward propagation of chaos results that are central in the proof of our main convergence result. We will start by proving the case with common noise and then we will come back to the case without common noise. The two proofs are similar, but the case with common noise is slightly more involved because the representing backward particle system if fully coupled with a forward process.

### 5.1 Proof of Theorem 2.11: The common noise case

Consider an interacting particle system $(X^{i,n},Y^{i,n},Z^{ij,n},Z^{*i,n})$ with the processes $(Y^{1,n},Y^{2,n},\dots,Y^{n,n})$ evolving backward in time, and $(X^{1,n},X^{2,n},\dots,X^{n,n})$ evolving forward in time and characterizing the Nash equilibrium, i.e. such that

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{\pi}_{t}^{i,n} \displaystyle=\left(\Sigma_{t}^{i}{\Sigma_{t}^{i}}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\Sigma_{t}^{i}P_{t}^{i}\left(\begin{pmatrix}Z_{t}^{ii,n}\\
Z_{t}^{*i,n}\end{pmatrix}+\eta^{i}\theta_{t}^{i}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t\otimes\mathbb{P}\text{--a.s.}\quad\text{and}\quad V^{i,n}_{0}((\widetilde{\pi}^{j,n})_{j\neq i})=-\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{1}{\eta^{i}}(\xi^{i}-\rho\overline{\xi}^{i}-Y_{0}^{i,n})}\;\;\forall i\in\{1,\dots,n\}, $$

see Theorem 3.1. We can find functions $h$ and $g$ such that they satisfy the following FBSDEs:

$$ \begin{cases}\mathrm{d}X^{i,n}_{t}=h^{i}(t,Z^{ii,n}_{t},Z^{*i,n}_{t})\Big\{\theta_{t}^{i}\mathrm{d}t+\sigma_{t}^{i}\mathrm{d}W^{i}_{t}+\sigma_{t}^{*i}\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{t}\Big\},\quad X^{i,n}_{0}=\xi^{i}.\\
\mathrm{d}Y^{i,n}_{t}=-\Big\{g^{i}(t,Z^{ii,n}_{t},Z^{*i,n}_{t})+\frac{1}{2\eta^{i}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}|Z^{ij,n}_{t}|^{2}\Big\}\mathrm{d}t+\sum_{j=1}^{n}Z^{ij,n}_{t}\mathrm{d}W^{j}_{t}+Z_{t}^{*i,n}\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{t}\\
Y^{i,n}_{T}=\rho\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}^{n}(X^{j,n}_{T}-X_{0}^{j,n}).\end{cases} $$

Observe that due to the graph $(\lambda_{ij})_{1\leq i,j\leq n}$ , the particles in the above system are not indistinguishable as in the homogeneous case considered by Laurière and Tangpi [34, 35] and Possamaï and Tangpi [42]. Our goal here is to show that as the number of particles in the system approaches infinity, the above particle system converges to the infinite particle system $(X^{u},Y^{u},Z^{u},Z^{*u})_{0\leq u\leq 1}$ given by

$$ \begin{cases}\mathrm{d}X^{u}_{t}=h^{u}(t,Z^{u}_{t},Z^{*u}_{t})\Big\{\theta^{u}_{t}\mathrm{d}t+\sigma_{t}^{u}\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{t}+\sigma_{t}^{*u}\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{t}\Big\},\quad X^{u}_{0}=\xi^{u}.\\
\mathrm{d}Y^{u}_{t}=-g^{u}(t,Z^{u}_{t},Z^{*u}_{t})\mathrm{d}t+Z_{t}^{u}\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{t}+Z^{*u}_{t}\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{t}\\
Y_{T}^{u}=\mathbb{E}[\rho\int_{I}(X_{T}^{v})G(u,v)\mathrm{d}v\mid\mathcal{F}_{T}^{*}]-\int_{I}\rho X_{0}^{v}G(u,v)\mathrm{d}v.\end{cases} $$

As above, this system is understood in the sense that the mapping $(u,t,\omega)\mapsto(X^{u}_{t},Y^{u}_{t},Z^{u}_{t},Z^{*u}_{t})$ is measurable and for almost every $u\in I$ , we have $(X^{u},Y^{u},Z^{u},Z^{*u})\in\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{u})\times\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{u})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F}^{u})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{u})$ . In particular, if we consider a specific particle $u=\frac{i}{n}$ in the continuum, we will show that $(Y_{t}^{i,n},Z_{t}^{ii,n},Z_{t}^{*i,n})$ and $(Y_{t}^{\frac{i}{n}},Z_{t}^{\frac{i}{n}},Z_{t}^{\frac{i}{n}*})$ are “close” when $n\rightarrow\infty$ . We will consider the following assumption on the coefficients of the FBSDEs:

#### Condition 5.1.

$h^{u}:[0,T]\times\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $g^{u}:[0,T]\times\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ are two functions such that there exist nonnegative constants $\ell_{g}$ and $\ell_{h}$ , so that for almost every $u\in I$ , it holds

$$ \displaystyle|h^{u}(t,z,z^{*})-h^{u}(t,z^{\prime},z^{*^{\prime}})|\leq{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\ell_{h}}\big(\|z-z^{\prime}\|+\|z^{*}-z^{*^{\prime}}\|\big)\text{ and }\|h^{u}(t,x,z^{*})\|_{\infty}\leq\ell_{h}(1+\|z\|+|z^{*}|) $$

and

$$ \displaystyle|g^{u}(t,z,z^{*})-g^{u}(t,z^{\prime},z^{*^{\prime}})|\leq\ell_{g}(\|z-z^{\prime}\|+|z^{*}-z^{*^{\prime}}|) $$

for all $(t,z,z^{\prime},z^{*},z^{*^{\prime}})\in[0,T]\times(\mathbb{R}^{d})^{2}\times\mathbb{R}^{2}$ .

#### Remark 5.2.

Recall that we use the same probability setting as described in Remark 2.10. In other words, the indices in (5.2) should be considered as $\frac{i}{n}$ . Further recall the link betwee $\lambda_{ij}$ and $\beta_{n}>0$ and the graphon $G$ is made in Condition 2.9.

Theorem 2.11. $(i)$ is then a direct corollary of the following theorem:

#### Theorem 5.3.

$$ \tau_{k}:=\inf\bigg\{s\geq t:\sup_{r\in[t,s]}|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{r}^{i,n}|^{2}+\int_{t}^{s}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\big(\|\Delta Z^{ij,n}_{r}\|^{2}+\|\Delta Z^{jj,n}_{r}\|+\|\Delta Z^{*j,n}_{r}\|^{2}+\|h^{j}(r,Z^{jj,n}_{r},Z^{*j,n}_{r})\|^{2}\big)\mathrm{d}r\geq k\bigg\}\wedge T. $$

Observe that $(\tau_{k})_{k}$ depends on $i$ and $n$ , but this dependence will be omitted to simplify notation. Since $(X^{i,n},Y^{i,n},Z^{ij,n},Z^{*i,n})\in\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{n})\times\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{n})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F}^{n})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{n})$ and $(X^{u},Y^{u},Z^{u},Z^{*u})\in\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{u})\times\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{u})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F}^{u})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F}^{u})$ it follows that for each $n$ and $i$ , $\tau_{k}$ converges to $T$ $\mathbb{P}$ -a.s as $k\rightarrow\infty$ . Furthermore, put

$$ \Gamma^{i,n}_{s}:=\rho\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}^{n}h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\cdot\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}-\rho\mathbb{E}\Big[\int_{I}h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\cdot\theta^{v}_{s}G(\frac{i}{n},v)\mathrm{d}v\big|\mathcal{F}^{*}_{T}\Big], $$

and

$$ \Gamma^{*i,n}_{s}:=\rho\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}^{n}h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\cdot\sigma^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s}-\rho\mathbb{E}\Big[\int_{I}h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\cdot\sigma^{*v}_{s}G(\frac{i}{n},v)\mathrm{d}v\big|\mathcal{F}^{*}_{T}\Big]. $$

Now, applying Itô’s formula to $|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{t}^{i,n}|^{2}$ , we get

$$ \displaystyle|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{t}^{i,n}|^{2}+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\Big(\sum\limits_{j=1}^{n}\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ij,n}_{s}\|^{2}+\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}\|^{2}\Big)\,\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle=|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k}}^{i,n}|^{2}+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\bigg(g^{i}(s,Z^{ii,n}_{s},Z^{*i,n}_{s})-g^{\frac{i}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{i}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{i}{n}}_{s})+\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\|Z_{s}^{ij,n}\|^{2}\bigg)\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\quad+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}^{i,n}_{s}\rho\sum_{j\neq i}\lambda_{ij}^{n}\theta^{j}_{s}\Big(h^{j}(s,Z^{jj,n}_{s},Z^{*j,n}_{s})-h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\Big)\,\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\quad+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\Gamma_{s}^{i,n}\mathrm{d}s-\sum_{j=1}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ij,n}_{s}\cdot\mathrm{d}W^{j}_{s}-\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{s}. $$

Recall that $\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ij,n}=\Delta Z^{ij,n}-\frac{\rho}{n\beta_{n}}\lambda_{ij}\sigma^{j}h^{j}(Z^{jj,n},Z^{*j,n})$ for $i\neq j$ and $\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ii,n}=\Delta Z^{ii,n}$ . Equation 5.8 now takes the form

$$ \displaystyle|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{t}^{i,n}|^{2}+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\Big(\sum\limits_{j=1}^{n}\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ij,n}_{s}\|^{2}+\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}\|^{2}\Big)\,\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle=|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k}}^{i,n}|^{2}+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\left(g^{i}(s,Z^{ii,n}_{s},Z^{*i}_{s})-g^{\frac{i}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{i}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{i}{n}}_{s})\right)\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\quad+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}^{i,n}_{s}\rho\sum_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}^{n}\theta^{j}_{s}\Big(h^{j}(s,Z^{jj,n}_{s},Z^{*j,n}_{s})-h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\Big)\,\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\quad+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\Gamma_{s}^{i,n}\mathrm{d}s+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\Gamma_{s}^{*i,n}\mathrm{d}s+\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\rho\lambda_{ij}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}h^{j}(s,Z_{s}^{jj,n},Z_{s}^{*j,n})\sigma_{s}^{j}\cdot\Delta Z_{s}^{ij,n}\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\quad-\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ij,n}_{s}\cdot\Big(\mathrm{d}W^{j}_{s}-\Delta Z_{s}^{ij,n}\mathrm{d}s\Big)-\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\Delta Z^{ii,n}_{s}\cdot\mathrm{d}W_{s}^{i}-\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{s}. $$

Let $\mathbb{Q}$ be the probability measure with density

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{Q}}{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}= \displaystyle\exp\Bigg(\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\Delta Z_{s}^{ij,n}\cdot\mathrm{d}W_{s}^{j}-\frac{1}{2}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\|\Delta Z_{s}^{ij,n}\|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\Bigg). $$

The probability measure $\mathbb{Q}$ depends on $i$ and $n$ , but its density has second moment bounded by a constant $C_{k}$ depending on $k$ , but not on $i$ and $n$ . Taking conditional expectation under $\mathbb{Q}$ with respect to $\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}$ in (5.9), we obtain the following:

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}&|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{t}^{i,n}|^{2}+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\Big(\sum\limits_{j=1}^{n}\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ij,n}_{s}\|^{2}+\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}\|^{2}\Big)\,\mathrm{d}s\Big|\mathcal{F}^{n}_{t}\bigg]\\
&\leq\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\left[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k}}^{i,n}|^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\right]+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\frac{2\ell_{g}^{2}}{\varepsilon}|\Delta\mathcal{Y}^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}+\varepsilon|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ii,n}_{s}|^{2}+\varepsilon|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}|^{2}\Big|\mathcal{F}^{n}_{t}\bigg]\\
&\quad+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\Big[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\Gamma_{s}^{i,n}\mathrm{d}s\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\Big]+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\Big[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}\Gamma_{s}^{*i,n}\mathrm{d}s\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\Big]\\
&\quad+C\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\left(|\Delta\mathcal{Y}^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}+\frac{\rho}{(n-1)^{2}\beta_{n}^{2}}\Big(\sum_{j=1}^{n}\lambda_{ij}^{2}\Big)\sum_{j\neq i}^{n}|\theta^{j}_{s}|^{2}\Big\|h^{j}(s,Z^{jj,n}_{s},Z^{*j,n}_{s})-h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\Big\|^{2}\right)\mathrm{d}s\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\bigg]\\
&\quad+C\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\rho\lambda_{ij}^{n}|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}|\|h^{j}(s,Z_{s}^{jj,n},Z_{s}^{*j,n})\sigma_{s}^{j}\cdot\Delta Z_{s}^{ij,n}\|\mathrm{d}s\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\bigg].\end{split} $$

Using $\mathbb{E}^{\mathfrak{P}}[\lambda^{2}_{ij}]\leq\beta_{n}$ and by definition of the stopping time $\tau_{k}$ , this estimate can be simplifed to

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}&|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{t}^{i,n}|^{2}+(1-\varepsilon)\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\Big(\sum\limits_{j=1}^{n}\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ij,n}_{s}\|^{2}+\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}\|^{2}\Big)\,\mathrm{d}s\big|\mathcal{F}^{n}_{t}\bigg]\\
&\leq\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\left[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k}}^{i,n}|^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\right]+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\Big(1+\frac{2\ell_{g}^{2}}{\varepsilon}\Big)|\Delta\mathcal{Y}^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\big|\mathcal{F}^{n}_{t}\bigg]\\
&\quad+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}|\Big(|\Gamma_{s}^{i,n}|+|\Gamma_{s}^{*i,n}|\Big)\mathrm{d}s\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\bigg]+\frac{C_{\rho,\theta,h,k}}{(n-1)\beta_{n}}\\
&\quad+C\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\rho\lambda_{ij}^{n}|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}|\|h^{j}(Z_{s}^{jj,n},Z_{s}^{*j,n})\sigma_{s}^{j}\cdot\Delta Z_{s}^{ij,n}\|\mathrm{d}s\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\bigg].\end{split} $$

Applying Young’s inequality and recalling the definition of $\tau_{k}$ , the last term above can be estimated as

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\Bigg[\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n} \displaystyle\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\rho\lambda_{ij}^{n}|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{s}^{i,n}|\|h^{j}(Z_{s}^{jj,n},Z_{s}^{*j,n})\sigma_{s}^{j}\cdot\Delta Z_{s}^{ij,n}\|\mathrm{d}s\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\Bigg] \displaystyle\leq\frac{\rho\|\sigma\|_{\infty}}{(n-1)\beta_{n}}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\sup_{t\leq s\leq\tau_{k}}|\Delta\mathcal{Y}^{i,n}_{s}|\bigg(\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\sum_{j\neq i}^{n}\|h^{j}(s,Z^{jj,n}_{s},Z^{*j,n}_{s})\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s+\sum_{j\neq i}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\|\Delta Z^{ij,n}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg)\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\frac{C_{\rho,\sigma,h,T,k}}{(n-1)\beta_{n}}. $$

Thus, choosing $\varepsilon<1$ and subsequently using in (5.10) Gronwall’s inequality, taking expectation with respect to $\mathbb{P}$ , Cauchy–Schwarz inequality and Doob’s inequality, we are left with

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Big[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{t}^{i,n}|^{2}\Big] \displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\bigg[\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\Big[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k}}^{i,n}|^{2}\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\Big]\bigg]+C_{k,T}\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{Q}}{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}\Big)^{4}\Big]^{\frac{1}{4}}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}|\Gamma_{s}^{i,n}|^{2}+|\Gamma^{*i,n}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]^{\frac{1}{2}}+\frac{C_{\rho,\sigma,\theta,h,T,k}}{(n-1)\beta_{n}}. $$

Observe that using again Cauchy–Schwarz we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\bigg[\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\Big[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k}}^{i,n}|^{2}\big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\Big]\bigg] \displaystyle\leq C\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{Q}}{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}\Big)^{2}\Big]^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathbb{E}\Big[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k}}|^{4}\Big]^{\frac{1}{2}}. $$

To proceed, first notice that for every $n$ , we have that $(|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k}}^{i,n}|^{4})_{k\geq 1}$ converges to $0$ in probability as $k\rightarrow\infty$ almost surely, since $\tau_{k}$ converges to $T$ $\mathbb{P}$ -a.s . There thus exists a fast sub-sequence $\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k,m}}^{i,n}$ such that

$$ \mathbb{P}(|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k,m}}^{i,n}|^{4}>\varepsilon)\leq\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-k^{3}}}{m}. $$

Therefore, for every $\varepsilon>0$ we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\big[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k,m}}^{i,n}|^{4}\big]=\mathbb{E}\Big[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k,m}}^{i,n}|^{4}\delta_{\{|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k,m}}^{i,n}|^{4}\leq\varepsilon\}}\Big]+\mathbb{E}\Big[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k,m}}^{i,n}|^{4}\delta_{\{|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{\tau_{k,m}}^{i,n}|^{4}>\varepsilon\}}\Big]\leq\varepsilon+k^{2}\cdot\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-k^{3}}}{m}. $$

Our definition of $\tau_{k}$ implies that all moments of $\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{Q}}{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}$ are upper bounded by $e^{Ck^{2}}$ for some constant $C>0$ independent of $k$ . Thus, coming back to (5.12) we continue the estimation as

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Big[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{t}^{i,n}|^{2}\Big] \displaystyle\leq\mathrm{e}^{Ck^{2}}\Big(\varepsilon+k^{2}\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-k^{3}}}{m}\Big)^{\frac{1}{2}}+\frac{C_{\rho,\sigma,\theta,h,T,k}}{(n-1)\beta_{n}}+C_{k,T}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}|\Gamma^{*i,n}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]^{\frac{1}{2}}+C_{k,T}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]^{\frac{1}{2}}. $$

Applying Lemma 5.4, first fix $k$ and let $n\rightarrow\infty$ , followed by letting $m\rightarrow\infty$ and $\varepsilon\to 0$ , we conclude that

$$ \mathbb{E}\Big[|\Delta\mathcal{Y}_{t}^{i,n}|^{2}\Big]\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0. $$

In particular, starting with $t=0$ , it follows that the sequence $(\Delta\mathcal{Y}^{i,n}_{0})_{n\geq 1}$ converges to zero, and since $\Delta\mathcal{Y}^{i,n}_{0}=\Delta Y^{i,n}_{0}$ , we obtain Equation 5.4.

Let us now turn to the convergence of the control processes. By Equation 5.10, Equation 5.14, Cauchy–Schwarz inequality and the above estimates we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k,m}}\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ii,n}_{s}\|+\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}\|\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq T\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Big(\frac{\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{Q}}{\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}\Big)^{2}\bigg]^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k,m}}\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ii,n}_{s}\|^{2}+\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg]^{\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\leq T\cdot\mathrm{e}^{Ck^{2}}\bigg\{\varepsilon+k^{2}\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-k^{3}}}{m}+\frac{C_{h,\theta,T,k}}{(n-1)\beta_{n}}+C_{k,T}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}|\Gamma^{*i,n}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]^{\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\quad+C_{k,T}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]^{\frac{1}{2}}\bigg\}^{\frac{1}{2}}. $$

Using Lemma 5.4, first fix $k$ and let $n\rightarrow\infty$ , followed by letting $m\rightarrow\infty$ and $\varepsilon\to 0$ , we conclude that, up to a subsequence, it holds

$$ \lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ii,n}_{s}\|\delta_{\{s\leq\tau_{k,m}\}}+\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}\|\delta_{\{s\leq\tau_{k,m}\}}=0\quad\mathbb{P}\text{--a.s.; }\text{ for a.e. }s\in[t,T]. $$

Since $\mathbb{P}(\tau_{k,m}\geq t)=1$ , this shows that

$$ \|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ii,n}_{t}\|+\|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{t}\|\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0\quad\mathbb{P}\text{--a.s.} $$

By the identity $\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{ii,n}=\Delta Z^{ii,n}$ , we have thus obtained that $(\Delta Z^{ii,n}_{t})_{n\geq 1}$ converges to zero. For the convergence of $\Delta Z^{*i,n}_{t}$ , observe that

$$ \displaystyle|\Delta Z^{*i,n}_{s}| \displaystyle\leq|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}|+|\Gamma^{*i,n}_{s}|+\frac{\rho}{n\beta_{n}}\sum_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}|\sigma^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s}|\Big|h^{j}(s,Z^{jj,n}_{s},Z^{*j,n}_{s})-h^{j}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\Big| \displaystyle\leq|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}|+|\Gamma^{*i,n}_{s}|+\rho\|\sigma^{*i}\|_{\infty}\ell_{h}\frac{1}{(n-1)\beta_{n}}\sum_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}\Big(\|\Delta Z^{jj,n}_{s}\|+|\Delta Z^{*j,n}_{s}|\Big). $$

Thus,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{\tau_{k,m}}|\Delta Z^{*i,n}_{s}|\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{\tau_{k,m}}|\Delta\mathcal{Z}^{*i,n}_{s}|^{2}+|\Gamma^{*i,n}_{s}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg]+\frac{C_{\rho,\sigma^{*},h,k}}{(n-1)\beta_{n}}. $$

Therefore, arguing as above and using again Lemma 5.4 we have that, up to a subsequence,

$$ \|\Delta Z^{*i,n}_{t}\|\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0\quad\mathbb{P}\text{--a.s.} $$

Therefore, Equation 5.5 follows by dominated convergence. This concludes the proof. ∎

#### Lemma 5.4.

Under the conditions of Theorem 5.3, it holds

$$ \mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}|\Gamma_{s}^{*i,n}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]+\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}|\Gamma_{s}^{i,n}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0\quad\text{for every }i\in\mathbb{N}^{*}. $$

#### Proof.

We will consider only the term $\Gamma^{i,n}$ ; the term $\Gamma^{*i,n}$ is dealt with similarly. Using Condition 2.9, especially that $\lambda_{ij}$ are i.i.d. and independent of $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ and $(W^{1},\dots,W^{n},W^{*})$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2} \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\bigg|\frac{1}{(n-1)\beta_{n}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}h^{j}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\cdot\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}-\mathbb{E}\Big[\int_{I}h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\cdot\theta^{v}_{s}G(\frac{i}{n},v)\mathrm{d}v\big|\mathcal{F}^{*}_{T}\Big]\bigg|^{2} \displaystyle\leq 2\mathbb{E}\bigg|\frac{1}{n-1}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\left(\frac{\lambda_{ij}}{\beta_{n}}h^{j}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}-h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},\frac{j}{n})\right)\bigg|^{2} \displaystyle\quad+2\mathbb{E}\bigg|\frac{1}{n-1}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},\frac{j}{n})-\mathbb{E}\Big[\int_{I}h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\cdot\theta^{v}_{s}G(\frac{i}{n},v)\mathrm{d}v\big|\mathcal{F}^{*}_{T}\Big]\bigg|^{2} \displaystyle\leq\frac{C_{\theta}}{(n-1)^{2}\beta_{n}^{2}}\mathrm{Var}(\lambda_{ij})\mathbb{E}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\big|h^{j}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\big|^{2} \displaystyle\quad+4\mathbb{E}\bigg|\frac{1}{n}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},\frac{j}{n})-\mathbb{E}\Big[\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},\frac{j}{n})\big|\mathcal{F}^{*}_{T}\Big]\bigg|^{2} \displaystyle\quad+\mathbb{E}\bigg|\mathbb{E}\Big[\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},\frac{j}{n})\big|\mathcal{F}^{*}_{T}\Big]-\mathbb{E}\Big[\int_{I}h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\cdot\theta^{v}_{s}G(\frac{i}{n},v)\mathrm{d}v\big|\mathcal{F}^{*}_{T}\Big]\bigg|^{2}. $$

Using that the step function $F^{n}_{s}(u)$ given by

$$ F^{n}_{s}(u):=\sum_{j=1}^{n}h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}\delta_{\{u\in(\frac{j}{n},\frac{j+1}{n}]\}} $$

approximates the function $F_{s}:v\mapsto h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\cdot\theta^{v}_{s}$ in $L^{2}(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\mu)$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2} \displaystyle\leq\frac{C_{\theta}}{(n-1)^{2}\beta_{n}^{2}}\mathrm{Var}(\lambda_{ij})\mathbb{E}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\big|h^{j}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\big|^{2} \displaystyle\quad+\frac{4}{(n-1)^{2}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\mathbb{E}\bigg|\Big(h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}-\mathbb{E}\big[h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}\big|\mathcal{F}^{*}_{T}\big]\bigg|^{2} \displaystyle\quad+\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Big|\int_{I}F^{n}_{s}(v)G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)\,\mathrm{d}v-\int_{I}h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\cdot\theta^{v}_{s}G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)\mathrm{d}v\Big|^{2}\Big] \displaystyle\quad+\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big|\int_{I}h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\cdot\theta^{v}_{s}G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)\mathrm{d}v-\int_{I}h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\cdot\theta^{v}_{s}G(\frac{i}{n},v)\mathrm{d}v\Big|^{2}\Big] \displaystyle\leq\frac{C_{\theta}}{(n-1)^{2}\beta_{n}^{2}}\mathbb{E}\Big|\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}(\lambda_{ij}-\mathbb{E}[\lambda_{ij}])h^{j}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\Big|^{2}+\frac{C_{\theta}}{(n-1)^{2}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\mathbb{E}\Big|\Big(h^{\frac{j}{n}}(s,Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s},Z^{*\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\Big|^{2} \displaystyle\quad+\|F^{n}_{s}-F_{s}\|_{L^{2}(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\mu)}+C_{\theta}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{I}\|h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\|^{2}\Big(G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)-G(\frac{i}{n},v)\Big)^{2}\,\mathrm{d}v\bigg]. $$

Because the Lipschitz constants of $h^{u}$ and $g^{u}$ do not depend on $u$ , standard FBSDE estimates show that $\sup_{u\in I}\|(Z^{u},Z^{*u})\|_{\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d+1},\mathbb{F}^{u})}<\infty$ . Hence, integrating on both sides above and using Condition 5.1, we have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\big(\frac{C_{h,\theta,T}}{(n-1)\beta_{n}^{2}}+\frac{C_{\theta}}{(n-1)}\big)\big(\sup_{u\in I}\|(Z^{u},Z^{*u})\|_{\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d+1},\mathbb{F}^{u})}+1\big)+C_{T}\|F^{n}_{s}-F_{s}\|_{L^{2}(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\mu)} \displaystyle\quad+\ell_{h}^{2}C_{\theta}\big(\sup_{u\in I}\|(Z^{u},Z^{*u})\|_{\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d+1},\mathbb{F}^{u})}+1\big)\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\int_{I}\Big(G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)-G(\frac{i}{n},v)\Big)^{2}\,\mathrm{d}v \displaystyle\leq\frac{C_{h,\theta,T,Z}}{(n-1)\beta_{n}^{2}}+\frac{C_{\theta,Z}}{(n-1)}+C_{T}\|F^{n}_{s}-F_{s}\|_{L^{2}(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\mu)} \displaystyle\quad+\ell_{h}^{2}C_{\theta,Z}\int_{I}\int_{I}\Big(G_{n}(\frac{\lfloor nu\rfloor}{n},v)-G(\frac{\lfloor nu\rfloor}{n},v)\Big)^{2}\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \displaystyle\leq\frac{C_{h,\theta,T,Z}}{(n-1)\beta_{n}^{2}}+\frac{C_{\theta,Z}}{(n-1)}+C_{T}\|F^{n}_{s}-F_{s}\|_{L^{2}(I,\mathcal{B}(I),\mu)}+\ell_{h}^{2}C_{\theta,Z}\|G_{n}-G\|_{2}^{2}. $$

Therefore, since $n\|G_{n}-G\|^{2}_{2}\to 0$ , it follows that for each $i$ , we have

$$ \mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}|\Gamma_{s}^{i,n}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0. $$

∎

#### Remark 5.5.

If the function $h$ is bounded (which is the case when the graphon equilibrium $(\widetilde{\pi}^{u})_{u\in I}$ is bounded), it is enough the require that $n\|G_{n}-G\|_{\Box}\to 0$ , which is weaker that $\mathbb{L}^{2}$ –convergence. This is due to the fact that the last term in Equation 5.15 can be estimated as

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg(\int_{I}h^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s},Z^{*v}_{s})\cdot\theta^{u}_{s}\Big(G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)-G(\frac{i}{n},v)\Big)\,\mathrm{d}v\bigg)^{2}\bigg] \displaystyle\leq C_{h,\theta}\bigg|\int_{I}\Big(G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)-G(\frac{i}{n},v)\Big)\,\mathrm{d}v\bigg|^{2}. $$

Taking the average, we obtain the following estimation

$$ \displaystyle\bigg(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\Big|\int_{I}G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)-G(\frac{i}{n},v)\mathrm{d}v\Big|\bigg)^{2}=\bigg(\int_{I}\Big|\int_{I}\Big(G_{n}(\frac{\lceil nu\rceil}{n},v)-G(\frac{\lceil nu\rceil}{n},v)\Big)\mathrm{d}v\Big|\mathrm{d}u\bigg)^{2}\leq 4\|G_{n}-G\|^{2}, $$

where $\|G\|$ is the so–called operator norm given by

$$ \|G\|:=\sup_{\|h\|_{\infty}\leq 1}\int_{I}\bigg|\int_{I}h(u)G(u,v)\,\mathrm{d}v\bigg|\,\mathrm{d}u. $$

It follows from Lovàsz [36, Lemma 8.11] that the $\|G\|_{\Box}$ and $\|G\|$ are equivalent norms. Therefore the last term in (5.16) can be replaced by $\ell_{h}^{2}C_{\theta,Z}\|G_{n}-G\|_{\Box}^{2}$ .

### 5.2 Proof of Theorem 2.11: The non–common noise case

Let us not present the proof of Theorem 2.11. $(ii)$ . Throughout this subsection, we assume $\sigma^{*u}=0$ for all $u\in I$ . By Theorem 3.1 and Remark 3.3, the Nash equilibrium $(\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n})_{i\in\{1,\dots,n\}}$ is characterized by the BSDE 3.5. That is, it holds

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{\pi}^{i,n}_{t}=(\sigma_{t}^{i})^{-1}P_{t}^{i}\left({Z_{t}^{ii}+\eta^{i}\theta_{t}^{i}}\right)\quad\text{and}\quad V_{0}^{i,n}((\widetilde{\pi}^{j,n})_{j\neq i})=-e^{-\frac{1}{\eta_{i}}(\xi^{i}-\rho\overline{\xi}^{i}-Y_{0}^{i})}\quad\mathbb{P}\otimes\mathrm{d}t\text{--a.s.} $$

with $(Y^{i,n},Z^{ij,n})_{(i,j)\in\{1,\dots,n\}^{2}}$ solving BSDE 3.5. Moreover, by Corollary 3.5 and Proposition 6.2, there is a graphon equilibrium $(\widetilde{\pi}^{u})_{u\in I}$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{\pi}^{u}_{t}=(\sigma_{t}^{u})^{-1}P_{t}^{u}\left({Z_{t}^{u}+\eta^{u}\theta_{t}^{u}}\right)\,\,\mathrm{d}t\otimes\mu\boxtimes\mathbb{P}\text{--a.s.}\text{ and}\quad V_{0}^{u,G}=-\exp\Big(-\frac{1}{\eta^{u}}\Big(\xi^{u}-\int_{I}\mathbb{E}[\rho\xi^{v}]G(u,v)\mathrm{d}v-Y_{0}^{u}\Big)\Big) $$

with $(Y^{u},Z^{u})_{u\in I}$ solving Equation 3.10. It thus suffices to show that

$$ \big|Y^{i,n}_{0}-Y^{\frac{i}{n}}_{0}\big|^{2}+\big|Z^{ii,n}_{t}-Z^{\frac{i}{n}}_{t}\big|^{2}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0\quad\,\mathrm{d}t\otimes\mathbb{P}\text{--a.s.} $$

Let us put $\Delta Y^{i,n}:=Y^{i,n}-Y^{\frac{i}{n}}$ and $\Delta Z^{ij,n}:=Z^{ij,n}-Z^{\frac{i}{n}}\delta_{\{i=j\}}$ . Let $t\in[0,T]$ be fixed and consider the stopping time

$$ \tau_{k}:=\inf\bigg\{s\geq t:\sup_{t\leq r\leq s}|\Delta Y^{i,n}_{r}|^{2}+\int_{t}^{s}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\|P^{j}_{r}(Z^{jj,n}_{r}+\eta^{j}\theta^{j}_{r})\|^{2}+\|\Delta Z^{jj,n}_{r}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\geq k\bigg\}\wedge T. $$

Observe that for each $i,n$ the sequence $(\tau_{k})_{k\geq 1}$ converges to $T$ $\mathbb{P}$ –a.s. Applying Itô’s formula to $\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}(\Delta Y^{i,n})^{2}$ for some $\kappa>0$ to be chosen, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{t})^{2} \displaystyle=\mathrm{e}^{\kappa\tau_{k}}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{\tau_{k}})^{2}+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}\Delta Y^{i,n}_{s}\Big\{\theta^{i}_{s}\cdot\Delta Z^{ii,n}_{s}+\frac{1}{2\eta^{i}}\Big(\big|(I-P^{i}_{s})(Z^{ii,n}_{s}+\eta^{i}\theta^{i}_{s})\big|^{2}-\big|(I-P^{\frac{i}{n}}_{t})(Z^{\frac{i}{n}}_{s}+\eta^{\frac{i}{n}}\theta^{\frac{i}{n}}_{s})\big|^{2}\Big)\Big\} \displaystyle\quad+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{i,n}_{s}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\big|Z^{ij,n}_{s}+\sigma^{j}\lambda^{n}_{ij}\rho P^{j}_{s}(Z^{jj,n}_{s}+\eta^{i}\theta^{i}_{s})\big|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\quad+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{i,n}_{s}\rho\Big\{\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda^{n}_{ij}P^{j}_{s}(Z^{jj,n}_{s}+\eta^{j}\theta^{j}_{s})\theta^{j}_{s}-\mathbb{E}\Big[\int_{I}P^{v}_{s}(Z^{v}_{s}+\eta^{v}\theta^{v}_{s})\theta^{v}_{s}G(u,v)\,\mathrm{d}v\Big]\Big\}\,\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\quad-\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\kappa\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{s})^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s-\sum_{j=1}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{ij,n}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s-\sum_{j=1}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{i,n}_{s}\Delta Z^{ij,n}_{s}\,\mathrm{d}W^{j}_{s}. $$

Let us introduce the measure $\mathbb{Q}$ with density

$$ \frac{\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{Q}}{\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}=\mathcal{E}\bigg(\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\big(\theta^{i}_{s}+\frac{1}{2\eta^{i}}\gamma_{s}(Z^{ii,n}_{s},Z^{\frac{i}{n}}_{s})\big)\,\mathrm{d}W^{i}_{s}+\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\Big(Z^{ij,n}_{s}+2Z^{ij,n}_{s}\sigma^{j}_{s}\lambda^{n}_{ij}\rho P^{j}_{s}(Z^{jj,n}_{s}+\eta^{j}\theta^{j}_{s})\Big)\,\mathrm{d}W^{j}_{s}\bigg), $$

where $\gamma_{s}$ is the (linearly growing) function such that

$$ \big|(I-P^{i}_{t})(Z^{ii,n}_{s}+\eta^{i}\theta^{i}_{s})\big|^{2}-\big|(I-P^{\frac{i}{n}}_{t})(Z^{\frac{i}{n}}_{s}+\eta^{\frac{i}{n}}\theta^{\frac{i}{n}}_{s})\big|^{2}=\gamma_{s}(Z^{ii,n}_{s},Z^{\frac{i}{n}}_{s})\Delta Z^{ii,n}_{s}. $$

This follows by Lipschitz–continuity of the projection operator since $A^{j}$ is convex (also recall the rebranding $i\equiv\frac{i}{n}$ ). Thus, by Girsanov’s theorem, the $\mathrm{BMO}$ martingale property of $Z^{\frac{i}{n}}$ , and square integrability of $Z^{ij,n}$ we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{t})^{2} \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa\tau_{k}}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{\tau_{k}})^{2}+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2e^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{i,n}_{s}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\rho^{2}\frac{\lambda_{ij}^{2}}{n^{2}\beta_{n}^{2}}\|\sigma^{j}_{s}\|^{2}\|P^{j}_{s}(Z^{jj,n}_{s}+\theta^{j}_{s}\eta^{j})\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\Big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\bigg] \displaystyle\quad+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{i,n}_{s}\rho\Big\{\frac{1}{n\beta_{n}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}P^{j}_{t}(Z^{jj,n}_{s}+\eta^{j}\theta^{j}_{s})\theta^{j}_{s}-\frac{1}{n\beta_{n}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}P^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}(Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}+\eta^{\frac{j}{n}}\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}\Big\}\,\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\qquad\qquad+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}2\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{i,n}_{s}\rho\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}-\kappa e^{\kappa s}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{s})^{2}-\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{ij,n}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\Big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\bigg] $$

where $\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}$ is the process given by

$$ \Gamma^{i,n}_{s}:=\frac{1}{n\beta_{n}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}P^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}(Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}+\eta^{\frac{j}{n}}\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}-\mathbb{E}\Big[\int_{I}P^{v}_{s}(Z^{v}_{s}+\eta^{v}\theta^{v}_{s})\theta^{v}_{s}G(\frac{i}{n},v)\,\mathrm{d}v\Big]. $$

Using Lipschitz–continuity of the projection operator and boundedness of $\Sigma$ , we continue the estimation as

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{t})^{2}+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\sum_{j=1}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{ij,n}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\Big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\bigg] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa\tau_{k}}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{\tau_{k}})^{2}+\frac{C_{k,\rho,\sigma}}{n^{2}\beta^{2}_{n}}+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}e^{\kappa s}\Big(\frac{C_{\theta,\sigma,\rho}}{\varepsilon}-\kappa\Big)|\Delta Y^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\Big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\bigg] \displaystyle\quad+\varepsilon\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Big\{\frac{1}{n\beta_{n}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}\|\Delta Z^{jj,n}_{s}\|\Big\}^{2}+\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\Big|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{n}\bigg], $$

where we also used Young’s inequality with some $\varepsilon>0$ . Choosing $\kappa>0$ large enough, and using Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, it follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{t})^{2}+\sum_{j=1}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{ij,n}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\Big[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa\tau_{k}}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{\tau_{k}})^{2}\Big]+\frac{C_{k,\rho}}{n^{2}\beta^{2}_{n}} \displaystyle\quad+\varepsilon\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\frac{1}{n\beta_{n}^{2}}\Big(\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda^{2}_{ij}\Big)\frac{1}{n}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\|\Delta Z^{jj,n}_{s}\|^{2}+\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\Big[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa\tau_{k}}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{\tau_{k}})^{2}\Big]+\frac{C_{k,\rho}}{n^{2}\beta^{2}_{n}}+\frac{C_{k,\kappa}}{n\beta_{n}}+\varepsilon\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg], $$

where we used the fact that $\lambda_{ij}$ is independent of $W^{1},\dots,W^{n}$ and $\mathbb{E}^{\mathfrak{P}}[\lambda^{2}_{ij}]\leq\beta_{n}$ , and definition of the stopping time $\tau_{k}$ . Because $(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{\tau_{k}})_{k\geq 1}$ converges to $0$ in $\mathbb{P}$ –probability and thus in $\mathbb{Q}$ –probability for each $n$ , we can find a fast sub–sequence $\Delta Y^{i,n}_{\tau_{k,m}}$ such that

$$ \mathbb{Q}\big(|\Delta Y^{i,n}_{\tau_{k,m}}|\geq\varepsilon\big)\leq\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-k^{2}}}{m}. $$

Thus, for every $\varepsilon>0$ , we have

$$ \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}[|\Delta Y^{i,n}_{\tau_{k,m}}|^{2}]\leq\varepsilon+k\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-k^{2}}}{m}. $$

Hence, using again definition of $\tau_{k}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{t})^{2}+\sum_{j=1}^{n}\int_{t}^{\tau_{k,m}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{ij,n}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\varepsilon+k\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-k^{2}}}{m}+\frac{C_{k,\rho,\sigma}}{n\beta_{n}}+\varepsilon\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg]. $$

Using Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, we further have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\bigg[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}|\Delta Y^{i,n}_{t}|+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k,m}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{ii,n}_{s}\|\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq 2T\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\frac{\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{Q}}{\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}\Big)^{2}\Big]^{1/2}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}(\Delta Y^{i,n}_{t})^{2}+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k,m}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{ii,n}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg]^{1/2} \displaystyle\leq C_{k}\bigg(\varepsilon+k\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-k^{2}}}{m}+\frac{C_{k,\rho,\sigma}}{n\beta_{n}}+\varepsilon\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k,m}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg]\bigg)^{1/2}. $$

We will show below that for each $k$ fixed

$$ \mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{t}^{\tau_{k,m}}|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg]\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0. $$

Thus, first taking the limit in $n$ , then in $m$ and and then letting $\varepsilon\to 0$ , it follows that

$$ \mathbb{E}\bigg[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}|\Delta Y^{i,n}_{t}|+\int_{t}^{\tau_{k,m}}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{ii,n}_{s}\|\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg]\xrightarrow[m,n\to\infty]{}0. $$

We thus obtain that $\Delta Y^{i,n}_{0}\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$ and, up to a subsequence,

$$ \|\Delta Z^{ii,n}_{s}\|\delta_{\{s\leq\tau_{k,m}\}}\xrightarrow[m,n\to\infty]{}0\quad\text{for almost every }s\in[t,T]\quad\mathbb{P}\text{--a.s. for a.e. }s\in[t,T]. $$

In particular, because $\mathbb{P}(\tau_{k,m}\geq 1)=1$ , $\Delta Z^{ii,n}_{t}\to 0$ $\mathbb{P}$ -a.s. as $n\to\infty$ .

Let us now come back to (5.18). Since the random variables $(Z^{u})_{u\in I}$ are e.p.i., it follows by the exact law of large numbers, see Sun [46, Corollary 3.10] that it holds

$$ \|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}\|\leq\Big\|\frac{1}{n\beta_{n}}\sum\limits_{j\neq i}^{n}\lambda_{ij}P^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}(Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}+\eta^{\frac{j}{n}}\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}-\int_{I}P^{v}_{s}(Z^{v}_{s}+\eta^{v}\theta^{v}_{s})\theta^{v}_{s}G(\frac{i}{n},v)\,\mathrm{d}v\Big\|. $$

Therefore, using triangular inequality and the fact that

$$ \int_{I}F^{n}_{s}(v)G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)(v)\,\mathrm{d}v=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}P^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}(Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}+\eta^{\frac{j}{n}}\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},\frac{j}{n}) $$

with

$$ F^{n}_{s}(u):=\sum_{j=1}^{n}P^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}(Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}+\eta^{\frac{j}{n}}\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}\delta_{\{u\in(\frac{j}{n},\frac{j+1}{n}]\}}, $$

it follows that

$$ \displaystyle\|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}\| \displaystyle\leq\Big\|\frac{1}{n\beta_{n}}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\lambda_{ij}P^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}(Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}+\eta^{\frac{j}{n}}\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}P^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}(Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}+\eta^{\frac{j}{n}}\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s})\theta^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},\frac{j}{n})\Big\| \displaystyle\quad+\Big\|\int_{I}F^{n}_{s}(v)G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)(v)\,\mathrm{d}v-\int_{I}F^{n}_{s}(v)G(\frac{i}{n},v)(v)\,\mathrm{d}v\Big\| \displaystyle\quad+\Big\|\int_{I}F^{n}_{s}(v)G(\frac{i}{n},v)\,\mathrm{d}v-\int_{I}P^{v}_{s}(Z^{v}_{s}+\eta^{v}\theta^{v}_{s})\theta^{v}_{s}G(\frac{i}{n},v)\,\mathrm{d}v\Big\|. $$

Proceeding as in the proof of Lemma 5.4, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{0}^{\tau_{k}}\|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mathrm{var}(\lambda_{ij})}{n\beta_{n}^{2}}\|\theta\|_{\infty}\Big(\|Z^{\frac{i}{n}}\cdot W^{\frac{i}{n}}\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}+C_{\theta,\eta}\Big)+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{I}\int_{0}^{\tau_{k}}\|F^{n}_{s}(v)\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\Big(G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)-G(\frac{i}{n},v)\Big)^{2}\,\mathrm{d}v\bigg] \displaystyle\quad+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{0}^{\tau_{k}}\int_{I}\|F^{n}_{s}(v)-P^{v}_{s}(Z^{v}_{s}+\eta^{v}\theta^{v}_{s})\theta^{v}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\frac{C_{\theta,\eta}}{n\beta^{2}_{n}}+\int_{I}\Big(G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)-G(\frac{i}{n},v)\Big)^{2}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}\|F^{n}_{s}(v)\|^{2}\bigg]\,\mathrm{d}v \displaystyle\quad+\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\frac{\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{Q}}{\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}\Big)^{2}\Big]^{1/2}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}\bigg(\int_{I}\|F^{n}_{s}(v)-P^{v}_{s}(Z^{v}_{s}+\eta^{v}\theta^{v}_{s})\theta^{v}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}v\bigg)^{2}\bigg]^{1/2}. $$

Since the intervals $(\frac{j}{n},\frac{j+1}{n}]$ form a partition of $I$ , and using linear growth of the projection operator, it follows that

$$ \|F^{n}_{s}(u)\|^{2}\leq\sum_{j=1}^{n}\|Z^{\frac{j}{n}}_{s}\|^{2}\delta_{u\in(\frac{j}{n},\frac{j+1}{n}]}+C_{\theta,A} $$

Thus, using the inequality $\|\cdot\|_{\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F}^{u})}\leq\|\cdot\|_{\mathbb{H}^{2}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F}^{u})}$ , that the BMO norm does not depend on the underlying measure and the fact that $\sup_{u\in I}\|Z^{u}\|_{\mathbb{H}^{2}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F}^{u})}<\infty$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}\|F^{n}_{s}(u)\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\sum_{j=1}^{n}\|Z^{\frac{i}{n}}\|_{\mathbb{H}^{2}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F}^{u})}\delta_{u\in(\frac{j}{n},\frac{j+1}{n}]}+C_{\theta,A} \displaystyle\leq C. $$

Hence, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{0}^{\tau_{k}}\|\Gamma^{i,n}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\frac{C_{\theta,\eta}}{n\beta^{2}_{n}}+C\int_{I}\Big(G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)-G(\frac{i}{n},v)\Big)^{2}\,\mathrm{d}v+C_{k}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}\|F^{n}_{s}-F_{s}\|_{L^{2}(I,\mu)}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg]^{1/2} $$

where $F_{s}(v):=P^{v}_{s}(Z^{v}_{s}+\eta^{v}\theta^{v}_{s})\theta^{v}_{s}$ . Since the sequence of step functions $F^{n}_{s}$ converges to $F$ in $L^{2}(I,\mu)$ , it follows by dominated convergence that, fixing $k$ , we have (5.18). The convergence to zero of the term $\int_{I}\Big(G_{n}(\frac{i}{n},v)-G(\frac{i}{n},v)\Big)^{2}\,\mathrm{d}v$ is proved as in at the end of the proof of Lemma 5.4. This concludes the proof.

## 6 Wellposedness of graphon McKean–Vlasov BSDEs and FBSDEs

We conclude the article with two existence results for graphon McKean–Vlasov (F)BSDEs used in the proof of existence of graphon equilibria. In the ensuing statements and proofs, we will use the space $\mathbb{S}^{p}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)$ defined as the space of families of processes $(Y^{u})_{u\in I}$ such that $(u,t,\omega)\mapsto Y^{u}$ is $\mathcal{I}\otimes\mathbb{F}$ –measurable and for almost every $u$ , it holds $Y^{u}\in\mathbb{S}^{p}(\mathbb{F}^{u},\mathbb{R}^{d})$ . This space is equipped with the norm

$$ \|Y\|_{\mathbb{S}^{p}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)}:=\int_{I}\|Y^{u}\|_{\mathbb{S}^{p}(\mathbb{F}^{u},\mathbb{R}^{d})}\mathrm{d}u $$

which makes it a Banach space. We similarly define $\mathbb{H}^{p}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)$ . We further denote by $\mathbb{H}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{F}^{u},\mathbb{R}^{d})$ the space of $\mathbb{F}^{u}$ –predictable processes $Z$ with values in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ such that the process $\int Z\mathrm{d}W^{u}$ is a $(\mathbb{P},\mathbb{F}^{u})$ –BMO martingale. The space $\mathbb{H}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)$ is defined analogously to $\mathbb{S}^{p}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)$ with the norm

$$ \|Z\|_{\mathbb{H}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)}:=\int_{I}\|Z^{u}\|_{\mathbb{H}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{F}^{u},\mathbb{R}^{d})}\mathrm{d}u. $$

### 6.1 Graphon McKean–Vlasov FBSDEs

We start by proving existence of the graphon McKean–Vlasov FBSDEs with Lipschitz coefficients. Observe that this is a system involving a continuum of coupled equation, where the coupling is due to the graphon term.

#### Proposition 6.1.

Assume that the functions $g:I\times[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ ; $b,h_{2}:I\times[0,T]\times\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $h_{1}:I\times[0,T]\times\Omega\times\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$ are Borel measurable and Lipschitz–continuous in the sense that

$$ \displaystyle|g^{u}(t,z,z^{*})-g^{u}(t,\bar{z},\bar{z}^{*})| \displaystyle\leq\ell_{g}(\|z-\bar{z}\|+|z^{*}-\bar{z}^{*}|) \displaystyle|b^{u}(t,z,z^{*})-b^{u}(t,\bar{z},\bar{z}^{*})| \displaystyle+\|h^{u}_{1}(t,z,z^{*})-h^{u}_{1}(t,\bar{z},\bar{z}^{*})\|+|h^{u}_{2}(t,z,z^{*})-h^{u}_{2}(t,\bar{z},\bar{z}^{*})|\leq\ell_{h}(\|z-\bar{z}\|+|z^{*}-\bar{z}^{*}|) $$

for some $\ell_{g},\ell_{h}>0$ and $(t,z,\bar{z},z^{*},\bar{z}^{*})\in[0,T]\times(\mathbb{R}^{d})^{2}\times\mathbb{R}^{2}$ , and $\int_{0}^{T}|g^{u}(t,0,0)|\mathrm{d}t<\infty$ . Further assume that we are given a family $(\xi^{u})_{u\in I}$ such that $\xi^{u}\in L^{2}(\mathcal{B}(I)\otimes\mathcal{F}^{u}_{0},\mu\otimes\mathbb{P})$ . Then, if $\rho<\frac{1}{2\ell_{h}}\mathrm{e}^{-(2\ell_{g}^{2}+\frac{1}{2})T}$ , the graphon system

$$ \begin{cases}\mathrm{d}X^{u}_{t}=b^{u}(t,Z^{u}_{t},Z^{*u}_{t})\mathrm{d}t+h^{u}_{1}(t,Z^{u}_{t},Z^{*u}_{t})\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{t}+h^{u}_{2}(t,Z_{t}^{u},Z^{*u}_{t})\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{t},\quad X^{u}_{0}=\xi^{u}.\\
\mathrm{d}Y^{u}_{t}=-g^{u}_{t}(Z^{u}_{t},Z^{*u}_{t})\mathrm{d}t+Z_{t}^{u}\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{t}+Z^{*u}_{t}\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{t}\\
Y_{T}^{u}=\mathbb{E}[\rho\int_{I}X_{T}^{v}G(u,v)\mathrm{d}v\mid\mathcal{F}_{T}^{*}]\end{cases} $$

admits a unique solution $(X^{u},Y^{u},Z^{u},Z^{*u})_{u\in I}\in\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)\times\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)$ .

#### Proof.

Let $(z^{u},z^{*u})_{u\in I}\in\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)$ be a given family of processes and consider $(X^{u},Y^{u},Z^{u},Z^{*}_{u})_{u\in I}$ given by

$$ \begin{cases}X^{u}_{t}:=\xi^{u}+\int_{0}^{t}b(s,z^{u}_{s},z^{*u}_{s})\mathrm{d}s+\int_{0}^{t}h_{1}(s,z^{u}_{s},z^{*u}_{s})\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{s}+\int_{0}^{t}h_{2}(s,z^{u}_{s},z^{*u}_{s})\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{s}\\
Y^{u}_{t}=\mathbb{E}\Big[\rho\int_{I}X^{v}_{T}G(u,v)\mathrm{d}v\Big|\mathcal{F}^{*}_{T}\Big]+\int_{t}^{T}g^{u}(s,Z^{u}_{s},Z^{*u}_{s})\mathrm{d}s-\int_{t}^{T}Z^{u}_{s}\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{s}-\int_{t}^{T}Z^{*u}_{s}\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{s}.\end{cases} $$

It follows by Stricker and Yor [45, Section 4] that $(u,t,\omega)\mapsto X^{u}_{t}$ is measurable, and thus that $\int_{I}X^{v}_{T}G(u,v)\mathrm{d}v$ is well–defined. Arguing as in the proof of [45, Section 4] (in particular using Picard iteration), one establishes that $(u,t,\omega)\mapsto(Y^{u}_{t},Z^{u}_{t},Z^{*u}_{t})$ is measurable. Moreover, since it is square–integrable, it follows by the standard result of Pardoux and Peng [40] on Lipschitz BSDEs that $(Y^{u},Z^{u})$ exists and is unique in $\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{F}^{u},\mathbb{R})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F}^{u},\mathbb{R}^{d})\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F}^{u},\mathbb{R})$ for almost every $u$ . Thus, the function

$$ \Psi((z^{u},z^{*u})_{u\in I}):=(Z^{u},Z^{*u})_{u\in I} $$

maps the Banach space $\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)$ into itself. It remains to show that $\Psi$ admits a unique fixed point.

Let $(z^{u},z^{*u})_{u\in I},(\bar{z}^{u},\bar{z}^{*u})_{u\in I}\in\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)$ be given. Put $\Psi((z^{u},z^{*u})_{u\in I})=(Z^{u},Z^{*u})_{u\in I}$ and $\Psi((\bar{z}^{u},\bar{z}^{*u})_{u\in I})=(\bar{Z}^{u},\bar{Z}^{*u})_{u\in I}$ such that $(X^{u},Y^{u},Z^{u},Z^{*}_{u})_{u\in I}$ and $(\bar{X}^{u},\bar{Y}^{u},\bar{Z}^{u},\bar{Z}^{*}_{u})_{u\in I}$ satisfy (6.2). Let us introduce the shorthand notation $\Delta X^{u}:=X^{u}-\bar{X}^{u}$ , $\Delta Y^{u}:=Y^{u}-\bar{Y}^{u}$ , $\Delta Z^{u}:=Z^{u}-\bar{Z}^{u}$ and $\Delta Z^{*u}:=Z^{*u}-\bar{Z}^{*u}$ . Given some constant $\kappa>0$ , we apply Itô’s formula to $\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}|\Delta Y^{u}_{t}|^{2}$ to obtain

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}|\Delta Y^{u}_{t}|^{2} \displaystyle\leq\mathrm{e}^{\kappa T}\rho^{2}\mathbb{E}\Big[\int_{I}\|\Delta X^{v}_{T}\|^{2}G(u,v)^{2}\mathrm{d}v\Big|\mathcal{F}^{*}_{T}\Big]+\int_{t}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\big(2\frac{\ell_{g}^{2}}{\varepsilon}-\kappa\big)|\Delta Y^{u}_{s}|^{2}+(\varepsilon-1)\int_{t}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\big(\|\Delta Z^{u}_{s}\|^{2}+|\Delta Z^{*u}_{s}|^{2}\big)\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\quad-\int_{t}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{u}_{s}\Delta Z^{u}_{s}\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{s}-\int_{t}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{u}_{s}\Delta Z^{*u}_{s}\mathrm{d}W^{*}_{s}. $$

Taking expectation on both sides and choosing $\kappa=2\ell_{g}^{2}/\varepsilon$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\bigg[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}|\Delta Y^{u}_{t}|^{2}+(1-\varepsilon)\int_{t}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{u}_{s}\|^{2}+\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Delta Z^{*u}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]\leq\mathrm{e}^{\kappa T}\rho^{2}\int_{I}\mathbb{E}\big[\|\Delta X^{v}_{T}\|^{2}\big]\mathrm{d}v. $$

On the other hand, applying Itô’s formula to $\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}\|\Delta X^{u}_{t}\|^{2}$ and using Lipschitz–continuity of $b^{u},h^{u}_{1}$ and $h^{u}_{2}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}\|\Delta X^{u}_{t}\|^{2}\big] \displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{t}2\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\ell_{h}(\|z^{u}_{s}-\bar{z}^{u}_{s}\|+|z^{*u}_{s}-\bar{z}^{*u}_{s}|)\|\Delta X_{s}^{u}\|+\ell_{h}^{2}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}(\|z^{u}_{s}-\bar{z}^{u}_{s}\|^{2}+|z^{*u}_{s}-\bar{z}^{*u}_{s}|^{2})\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\quad+\kappa\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta X^{u}_{s}\|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\bigg[(1+\kappa)\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta X_{s}^{u}\|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]+2\ell_{h}^{2}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\big(\|z^{u}_{s}-\bar{z}^{u}_{s}\|^{2}+|z^{*u}_{s}-\bar{z}^{*u}_{s}|^{2}\big)\mathrm{d}s\bigg], $$

where the last inequality follows from Young’s inequality. Thus, by Gronwall’s inequality, we have

$$ \mathbb{E}\big[\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}\|\Delta X^{u}_{t}\|^{2}\big]\leq 2\ell_{h}^{2}\mathrm{e}^{(\kappa+1)T}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{t}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\big(\|z^{u}_{s}-\bar{z}^{u}_{s}\|^{2}+|z^{*u}_{s}-\bar{z}^{*u}_{s}|^{2}\big)\mathrm{d}s\bigg]. $$

Thus, if $\varepsilon=1/2$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\int_{I}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{u}_{s}\|^{2}+\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Delta Z^{*u}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\bigg]\mathrm{d}u\leq 4\ell_{h}^{2}\mathrm{e}^{(4\ell_{g}^{2}+1)T}\rho^{2}\int_{I}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{0}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\big(\|z^{u}_{s}-\bar{z}^{u}_{s}\|^{2}+|z^{*u}_{s}-\bar{z}^{*u}_{s}|^{2}\big)\mathrm{d}s\bigg]\mathrm{d}u. $$

Thus, by the choice of $\rho$ and the Banach fixed point theorem, the mapping $\Psi$ admits a unique fixed point, implying that the graphon FBSDE (6.1) admits a unique solution in $\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)\times\mathbb{S}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)\times\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)$ . ∎

### 6.2 Graphon McKean–Vlasov BSDE

Let us now turn to the wellposedness of graphon McKean–Vlasov FBSDEs with Lipschitz–continuous coefficients.

#### Proposition 6.2.

Assume that the functions $g:I\times[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $f:I\times[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ are Borel–measurable and satisfy the locally Lipschitz and Lipschitz–continuity conditions

$$ |g^{u}(t,z)-g^{u}(t,z^{\prime})|\leq\ell_{g}(\|z\|+\|z^{\prime}\|)\|z-z^{\prime}\|\quad\text{and}\quad|g^{u}(t,z)|\leq\ell_{g}(1+\|z\|^{2}) $$

and

$$ |f^{u}(t,z)-f^{u}(t,z^{\prime})|\leq\ell_{f}\|z-z^{\prime}\|\quad\text{and}\quad|f^{u}(t,z)|\leq\ell_{f}(1+\|z\|) $$

for some constants $\ell_{g},\ell_{f}>0$ and every $(t,z,z^{\prime})\in[0,T]\times(\mathbb{R}^{d})^{2}$ and almost all $u\in I$ . Further assume that we are given $\mathcal{F}^{u}_{T}$ –measurable random variables $F^{u}$ such that $(u,\omega)\mapsto F^{u}$ is measurable and uniformly bounded. Then, the graphon system

$$ Y^{u}_{t}=F^{u}+\int_{t}^{T}\Big(g^{u}(s,Z^{u}_{s})+\int_{I}\mathbb{E}[f^{v}(s,Z^{v}_{s})]G(u,v)\mathrm{d}v\Big)\,ds-\int_{t}^{T}Z^{u}_{s}\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{s} $$

admits a unique solution $(Y^{u},Z^{u})_{u\in I}$ such that we have $(Y^{u},Z^{u})_{u\in I}\in\mathbb{S}^{\infty}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)\times\mathbb{H}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)$ and $\sup_{u\in I}\|Z^{u}\|_{\mathbb{H}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d})}<\infty$ .

#### Proof.

Let $(y^{u},z^{u})_{u\in I}\in\mathbb{S}^{\infty}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)\times\mathbb{H}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)$ be given and consider the (decoupled) quadratic BSDEs

$$ Y^{u}_{t}=F^{u}+\int_{t}^{T}\Big(g^{u}(s,Z^{u}_{s})+\int_{I}\mathbb{E}[f^{v}(s,z^{v}_{s})]G(u,v)\mathrm{d}v\Big)\,ds-\int_{t}^{T}Z^{u}_{s}\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{s}. $$

It follows by Hu et al. [25] that for almost every $u\in I$ , this equation admits a unique solution $(Y^{u},Z^{u})\in\mathbb{S}^{\infty}(\mathbb{F}^{u},\mathbb{R})\times\mathbb{H}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{F}^{u},\mathbb{R}^{d})$ . Moreover, it follows by the arguments of Stricker and Yor that $(u,t,\omega)\mapsto(Y^{u}_{t},Z^{u}_{t})$ is measurable. Thus, the function

$$ \Psi((y^{u},z^{u})_{u\in I}):=(Y^{u},Z^{u})_{u\in I} $$

is well–defined and maps the Banach space $\mathbb{S}^{\infty}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)\times\mathbb{H}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)$ into itself. It therefore remains to show that this mapping admits a unique fixed point.

Let $(y^{u},z^{u})_{u\in I},(\bar{y}^{u},\bar{z}^{u})_{u\in I}\in\mathbb{S}^{\infty}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R},I)\times\mathbb{H}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{R}^{d},I)$ be given and put $\Psi((y^{u},z^{u})_{u\in I})=(Y^{u},Z^{u})_{u\in I}$ and $\Psi((\bar{y}^{u},\bar{z}^{u})_{u\in I})=(\bar{Y}^{u},\bar{Z}^{u})_{u\in I}$ . Let $\kappa>0$ be a constant to be determined and let $\tau$ be an $\mathbb{F}^{u}$ –stopping time. Apply Itô’s formula to $\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}|\Delta Y^{u}_{t}|^{2}:=\mathrm{e}^{\kappa t}|Y^{u}_{t}-\bar{Y}^{u}_{t}|^{2}$ to obtain

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{e}^{\kappa\tau}|\Delta Y_{\tau}^{u}|^{2} \displaystyle=\int_{\tau}^{T}2\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{u}_{s}\Big(g^{u}(s,Z^{u}_{s})-g^{u}(s,\bar{Z}^{u}_{s})+\int_{I}\mathbb{E}[f^{v}(s,z^{v}_{s})-f^{v}(s,\bar{z}^{v}_{s})]G(u,v)\mathrm{d}v\Big)\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\quad-\kappa\int_{\tau}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Delta Y^{u}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s-\int_{\tau}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta Z^{u}_{s}\|^{2}\mathrm{d}s-\int_{t}^{T}2\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{u}_{s}\Delta Z^{u}_{s}\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{s} \displaystyle\leq\Big(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}-\kappa\Big)\int_{\tau}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Delta Y^{u}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s+\varepsilon\ell^{2}_{f}\int_{\tau}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\int_{I}\mathbb{E}[\|\Delta z^{u}_{s}\|^{2}]G(u,v)^{2}\mathrm{d}s-\int_{\tau}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Delta Z^{u}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s \displaystyle\quad-\int_{\tau}^{T}2\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\Delta Y^{u}_{s}\Delta Z^{u}_{s}\mathrm{d}W^{u,\mathbb{Q}}_{s} $$

where we used the short hand notation $\Delta Z^{u}:=Z^{u}-\bar{Z}^{u}$ and $\Delta z^{u}:=z^{u}-\bar{z}^{u}$ , and where $W^{u,\mathbb{Q}}$ is a Brownian motion under the probability measure

$$ \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{Q}}{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}:=\mathcal{E}\Big(\int_{0}^{\cdot}\beta^{u}(s,Z^{u}_{t},\bar{Z}^{u}_{t})\mathrm{d}W^{u}_{t}\Big) $$

with $\beta$ being a linearly growing function such that $g^{u}(s,z)-g^{u}(s,\bar{z})=\beta^{u}(s,z,\bar{z})\cdot(z-\bar{z})$ . Choose $\kappa$ such that $\kappa>\frac{1}{\varepsilon}$ . Taking conditional expectation on both sides yields

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{e}^{\kappa\tau}|\Delta Y_{\tau}^{u}|^{2}+\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{Q}}\bigg[\int_{\tau}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}|\Delta Z^{u}_{s}|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\Big|\mathcal{F}^{u}_{\tau}\bigg] \displaystyle\leq\varepsilon\ell_{f}^{2}\int_{I}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\int_{\tau}^{T}\mathrm{e}^{\kappa s}\|\Delta z^{v}_{s}\|^{2}\mathrm{d}s\Big|\mathcal{F}^{u}_{\tau}\bigg]\mathrm{d}v. $$

Taking the supremum over $\tau$ and integrating on both sides in $u$ therefore gives

$$ \|\Delta Y\|^{2}_{\mathbb{S}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F},I)}+\|\Delta Z\|^{2}_{\mathbb{H}^{2}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F},I)}\leq\varepsilon\ell_{f}^{2}\|\delta z\|^{2}_{\mathbb{H}^{2}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F},I)}, $$

and where we used the fact that the BMO norm does not depend on the underlying probability measure and $\|\cdot\|_{\mathbb{H}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F})}\leq\|\cdot\|^{2}_{\mathbb{H}^{2}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F})}$ . Choosing $\varepsilon>0$ small enough allows to conclude that $\Psi$ is a contraction, and thus it follows by the Banach fixed point theorem that $\Psi$ admits a unique fix point in $\mathbb{S}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{F},I)\times\mathbb{H}^{2}_{\mathrm{BMO}}(\mathbb{R}^{d},\mathbb{F},I)$ . ∎

## Abstract

Objective: This study aimed to investigate the diagnostic performance of CT myocardial perfusion imaging (CT-MPI)  in detecting myocardial ischemia in patients with intermediate coronary stenosis

(50%–70%) using fractional flow reserve (FFR) as the reference standards.

Methods: Consecutive patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) diagnosed using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were prospectively enrolled and scanned with adenosine-

stress dynamic CT-MPI and referred to invasive coronary angiography (ICA) and FFR within 10 days. The inclusion criteria were as follows: intermediate coronary artery stenosis confirmed using quantitative ICA,

and the FFR was measured to assess its hemodynamic significance.

Results: In 31 patients, intermediate stenosis was confirmed using ICA in 31 vessels, and FFR was

measured in these vessels. Based on the FFR results, 24 vessels were assessed as causing ischemia in 24 patients (FFR £ 0.80). On a per-vessel basis, the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive values (PPV)

and negative predictive values (NPV) and diagnostic accuracy of absolute myocardial blood flow (MBF) and relative MBF were 79.17%, 85.71%, 54.54%, 95%, and 80.65% and 95.83%, 85.71%, 85.71%, 95.83%,

and 93.55%, respectively. With FFR £ 0.8 as a positive event, the area under the curve (AUC) values for the qualitative (visual) assessment, absolute MBF, and relative MBF were found to be 0.601, 0.792, and

0.899, respectively. The relative MBF was higher than the qualitative assessment (P < 0.05). The AUC of the relative MBF value was higher than the absolute MBF value, but the difference was not statistically

significant (P = 0.0649). The absolute MBF cutoff value was 116.275 mL·100 mL-1·min-1, and the relative MBF cutoff value was 0.736.

Conclusion: The CT-MPI is feasible in detecting myocardial ischemia in patients with intermediate

coronary stenosis.

## Key Points

1. In patients with intermediate coronary artery disease (CAD), adenosine-stress dynamic CT-MPI can

reflect hemodynamic changes as confirmed using invasive FFR.

2. The area under the ROC curve of relative MBF in diagnosing the hemodynamic changes of

intermediate CAD was higher than that in qualitative assessment; however, it was only slightly higher

than that of the absolute MBF with no statistical difference. 3. For patients with intermediate CAD, the optimal cutoff values of the absolute and relative MBF for

hemodynamic changes were 116.275 ml·100 ml− 1·min− 1 and 0.736, respectively.

## Introduction

It is crucial to determine whether coronary artery disease (CAD) leads to myocardial ischemia for clinical decision-making processes. However, there is no linear relationship between the degree of vascular stenosis and the severity of myocardial ischemia, and there is uncertainty regarding whether intermediate


<!-- Page 4 -->


Page 4/17

CAD (50–70%) leads to myocardial ischemia1. Previous studies have reported that approximately onethird of patients with intermediate CAD have myocardial ischemia [1, 2]. Therefore, functional assessment of patients with intermediate CAD has important clinical implications for optimizing

revascularization strategies [3].

Currently, fractional flow reserve (FFR) is the gold standard for evaluating the hemodynamic significance of intermediate CAD, and it is also used as a guide to determine if revascularization should be performed. Recently, the guidelines for coronary intervention in Europe, USA, and China have listed FFR-guided

coronary revascularization as a class IA recommendation; however, the invasiveness and high cost of FFR examination render the application of this diagnostic technique difficult to popularize. Over the past decade, with the continuous development of CT technology, dynamic CT myocardial perfusion imaging (CT-MPI) has become a promising noninvasive method for evaluating hemodynamic changes in CAD [4–

6]. However, the application of stress dynamic CT-MPI in patients with intermediate CAD has not yet been elucidated. In this study, invasive coronary angiography (ICA) and FFR were used as reference standards to investigate the ability of stress dynamic CT-MPI to determine the hemodynamic significance of intermediate CAD as well as to preliminarily explore its quantitative indicators and cutoff values of

myocardial perfusion.

## Materials and Methods

## Patients

The study prospectively and consecutively enrolled patients with clinically suspected CAD who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), stress dynamic CT-MPI, ICA, and FFR within a period of 10 days from April 2019 to December 2021. Patients with intermediate CAD as confirmed using

quantitative ICA analysis who also underwent FFR were included in this study. The exclusion criteria were as follows: (1) poor quality of stress dynamic CT-MPI images; (2) history of coronary revascularization; (3) history of myocardial infarction; and (4) patients with suspected cardiomyopathy or microcirculatory dysfunction. This study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian

Medical University (PJ-XJS-2019-79). Patients and their families signed informed consent forms.
